newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-IDLE IDOL BAGGIO GETS CHANCE TO START.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IDLE IDOL BAGGIO GETS CHANCE TO START.

text.p: Idle idol Roberto Baggio won a chance to shine on Friday when sickness ruled striker Marco Simone out of AC Milan's weekend league match at Roma.
The Italian soccer league champions said Simone's absence, enforced by a stomach upset, meant Baggio would partner Liberian George Weah in attack in Saturday's game.
It will be the first match Baggio, world player of the year in 1993 and Italy's hero in the World Cup in 1994, has started since the season opener against Verona on September 8.
His call-up for Milan, where the Weah-Simone strike force has relegated him to expensive reserve, came on the day the "Divine Ponytail" told the world of soccer not to write him off.
He vowed to win back a place in Italy's line-up, from which he has been missing since September 1995, and return to playing regularly for his club.
Baggio, 29, told Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper in an interview he had "not even dreamed" of never returning to the national side, despite his long absence.

"I am the leading national goalscorer still playing," Baggio said. "I've scored 24 goals and I'm not 30 yet so why should I give up? No. It's still on my mind and I'm going to do everything to return."
He said the same ambition applied at AC Milan, where he came on as a substitute in his last game against Perugia on September 29 to score from a devastating free kick.

"I still train and behave as if I were playing every weekend and every game. You know what the problem is? Just one. If I were a foreigner nobody, or very few people, would have laid into me so heavily," Baggio said.
He said he would not think of his future until his contract with Milan, which he signed in 1995, expired next year, but a move abroad was out of the question.

Milan are second in the league, one point behind European Champions Juventus. Victory in Rome's Olympic stadium would put Milan top, at least for 24 hours. Juventus play Vicenza on Sunday with every hope of full points.
